key_insight: Tuna-2 replaces pretrained vision encoders with native pixel (patch) embeddings, using the same visual representation for both understanding and generation so the entire multimodal model can be trained end-to-end from raw pixels.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal systems use different visual representations for perception and generation (pretrained encoders vs. generation inputs), causing task misalignment and preventing fully end-to-end optimization from pixels.
method: Encode images directly with simple patch/pixel embedding layers rather than large pretrained vision encoders.

Use a single unified multimodal architecture that consumes pixel embeddings for both visual understanding (e.g., VQA, classification) and visual generation (e.g., captioning, multimodal generation), removing representational mismatch.
Train the model end-to-end from raw pixels to downstream outputs, simplifying the pipeline and enabling joint optimization of visual and language components.
impact: By unifying representations and enabling end-to-end training from pixels, Tuna-2 simplifies model design and reduces encoder–decoder misalignment—helpful for building more flexible, maintainable multimodal systems and for research on pixel-native multimodal learning.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline comparison: traditional pretrained-encoder → fusion → generator vs. Tuna-2 raw pixels → patch embeddings → single multimodal model.
Architecture diagram: image → patch embeddings → unified transformer → branching outputs (understanding & generation).
Benefits icons/chart: alignment, end-to-end training, simpler stack, fewer components.
Example input→output panel: raw image with generated caption and visual QA pair to show both tasks from same representation.
paper_title: Tuna-2: Pixel Embeddings Beat Vision Encoders for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Zhiheng Liu, Weiming Ren, Xiaoke Huang, Shoufa Chen, Tianhong Li
